text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated 5xxs on /v1/embeddings in eu-west-1. 5xx rate 18% over 5m. Error samples show 'incompatible_input_type: chat payload received for embedding model'. Fallback policy is routing to 'redwood-chat-v2-instruct' variant. Pager triggered.

Ava (oncall): taking pager. looking at metrics — lots of fallback churn and region failover activity. @Sam R were there recent alias/anchor changes for embeddings?

Sam R: I pushed an alias update ~15m ago to pin 'embed-prod' to version 'v2026-anchored'. I thought it was the new quantized embed model but looking now the alias points at a chat/instruct family variant. my fault.

Priya G: that explains the errors. embedding payloads hitting chat runtimes -> invalid interface -> 500s -> fallback triggers -> cross-region failover loops. EU clients get recycled to other regions and then fallback again.

Diego L: immediate options: 1) disable cross-region fallback for this alias, 2) unpin alias to last known-good embed version, 3) add a temporary reject rule for mismatched interface. Which is fastest?

Ava (oncall): disable fallback for embed-prod in eu-west-1 first, then unpin. @Marta can you run the CLI? also we should estimate customer impact and get a status page ready if >10% users affected.

Marta (eng-pager): running: ```redwoodctl routing set-fallback --alias embed-prod --mode none --region eu-west-1``` -> OK. Setting rollback of alias to previous version 'v2025-embed-q4' in 2m.

ops-bot: AUTOMATION: fallback mode set to 'none' for alias 'embed-prod' in eu-west-1 by Marta (eng-pager). Scheduling alias rollback.

Sam R: rolling back alias now: ```redwoodctl alias update embed-prod --version v2025-embed-q4``` -> DONE. Confirmed alias now points to embedding variant.

Priya G: observability update: 5xxs down from 18% -> 2% within ~90s after rollback. still seeing backlog due to cached routing entries and in-flight retries.

Ava (oncall): good containment. next safety step: block cross-interface fallback entirely for this alias so we don't thrash. also add a short TTL flush for routing caches.

Diego L: filing a config PR to make fallback policy interface-aware (prevent chat <-> embed cross-fallback). ETA 2 hours for code + review, will push hotfix if needed.

Marta (eng-pager): customer impact assessment: org-42 and org-88 reported degraded embeddings; estimated ~6k failed requests in last 30m, retry rate ~40%. No evidence of data exfiltration. preparing status page message.

Ava (oncall): followups: Sam to harden alias registry validation before deploy; Diego to add interface-compat checks in routing; Priya to sample failed payloads and coordinate with SDK; Marta to publish status and notify affected customers.

Sam R: creating internal ticket INC-4589 for alias validation and adding a pipeline gate. I'll also revert my deploy checklist to include a double-check for variant family.

Priya G: sampling logs show many clients still sending chat-style 'messages' field to the embeddings endpoint — looks like an SDK version mismatch in the wild. notifying SDK team after immediate mitigation.

Ava (oncall): @Sam R please open SDK issue and tag customers who sent example payloads. Ops: prepare brief customer outreach to org-42.

Marta (eng-pager): status.redwood.com update drafted: "Partial degradation of embeddings in EU has been mitigated by removing an incorrect alias pin and disabling cross-region fallback. Root cause: mis-anchored alias mapping to a chat variant. Investigating full root cause and next steps." Posting now.

ops-bot: NOTIFICATION: status.redwood.com incident-3625004321 posted. Severity P2.

Diego L: post-incident action items: - add interface compatibility check into routing fallback engine - implement per-route circuit-breaker on 5xx spikes - add alias deploy validation + automated rollback on spike >10% within 5m - add telemetry for alias changes to alert SRE teams faster.

Ava (oncall): monitoring looks stable for the 30m window. closing pager after 60m watch. schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow with SRE, routing, SDK, and platform teams. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
